narration_timeline.text: Why are these mallard ducklings moving together instead of scattering across the water?
A family can travel near the bank, where young birds remain close to the adults.
narration_timeline.scene: Mallard family swimming in a group.

narration_timeline.text: The ducklings paddle in short bursts, leaving ripples as they cross the surface, while other ducks remain nearby on the water.
narration_timeline.scene: Ducklings paddling; second water-family shot needs preview.

narration_timeline.text: Webbed feet push against the water, helping these birds move while their bodies float, even when the shoreline is uneven.
narration_timeline.scene: Adult mallard swimming and a second water shot, pending source-window check.

narration_timeline.text: A busy stretch of water still leaves the group room to turn and regroup.
narration_timeline.scene: Mallards on a populated pond; actual grouping to be verified.

narration_timeline.text: That moving cluster is a simple way for young ducks to keep traveling together.
narration_timeline.scene: Return to distinct family footage; must show young birds.
